faq.question: Do I really need a security audit?
faq.answer: If you store customer data, process payments or have GDPR obligations to meet — yes. If you work with enterprise clients, they'll typically ask for an audit or ISO 27001 certification. If you've already had an incident — definitely. Prevention beats cleaning up after a breach.

faq.question: How much does a security audit cost?
faq.answer: Web application audit: EUR 2000-5000. Infrastructure penetration testing: EUR 3000-8000. Full audit + remediation + ISO 27001 prep: EUR 15000-30000. It depends on complexity. We provide a fixed quote after a 1-hour scoping call.

faq.question: GDPR and ISO 27001 — what do they mean for my business?
faq.answer: GDPR: mandatory if you process personal data of EU citizens. Fines up to 4% of annual revenue. ISO 27001: international standard for information security, often required when selling to enterprise. Both require documentation, processes and concrete controls — not just "we had a policy in a drawer somewhere".

faq.question: What do we do if we've already been hacked?
faq.answer: 24/7 incident response. Step one: contain the impact (stop propagation). Step two: analyze what was lost (forensics). Step three: restore operations (backup, patch the vulnerability). Step four: report per GDPR (72-hour notification to the authority). Ideally though: call us BEFORE.

faq.question: Can't I just run penetration tests myself with Kali Linux?
faq.answer: For learning — yes. For actually uncovering the real vulnerabilities in your business — no, because you don't have the tools, the time and, most of all, the attacker mindset built up over years. Real penetration testing is a craft. Plus: your internal report isn't valid for compliance purposes.

faq.question: How long until we're "100% secure"?
faq.answer: "100% secure" doesn't exist — security is a continuous process. What we can promise: reducing risk by 80%+ in 90 days. Establishing a mature security program in 6-12 months. Maintaining it through continuous monitoring and annual audits.

faq.question: What is a smart contract and why would I need one?
faq.answer: A smart contract = code that runs automatically on a blockchain when predefined conditions are met. Examples: automatic payment when goods are delivered, NFT royalty distribution, staking/unstaking tokens, DAO voting. Useful when you want automation without intermediaries and full transparency.

faq.question: How much does smart contract development cost?
faq.answer: Simple smart contract (ERC-20 token, ERC-721 NFT): EUR 3000-8000. Complex smart contract (DeFi protocol, staking, lending): EUR 15000-40000. Recommended security audit: +EUR 5000-20000. The price reflects the risk — a bug in the code means permanently lost funds.

faq.question: Which blockchain should I pick — Ethereum, Polygon, Solana?
faq.answer: Ethereum: most secure and with the largest user base, but high fees. Polygon: nearly the same as Ethereum, but with fees under $0.01. Solana: very fast and cheap, but a smaller ecosystem. BSC: low fees, but centralized. Our recommendation: Polygon for most new projects.

faq.question: Why do I need a security audit?
faq.answer: Because smart contracts are immutable once deployed. A bug = permanently lost funds with no recovery. Famous examples: the DAO hack (USD 60M), Wormhole (USD 325M), Ronin (USD 625M). External audits are industry standard for any protocol with meaningful TVL.

faq.question: Can you add crypto payments to my website?
faq.answer: Yes. We use solutions like Coinbase Commerce, CoinPayments, BTCPay Server (self-hosted) or Stripe Crypto. You can accept Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins (USDC, USDT). Integration takes 1-3 weeks depending on requirements (KYC, fiat conversion invoicing).

faq.question: Is blockchain legal in my jurisdiction?
faq.answer: Building software is broadly legal everywhere; what varies is regulated financial activity (exchanges, custody, tokenization of securities) — that falls under your jurisdiction's laws and regulators. We work with specialized counsel when needed. For many common cases (NFTs, utility tokens, typical DeFi integrations), delivery is straightforward.
